brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray with at least four cells
requirements.evidence: 4 hex bases (piece:0,0,0; piece:0,1,0; piece:1,-1,0; piece:1,0,0) arranged as compact cluster ~364x467mm

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a draining bin
requirements.evidence: 4 × hex-bin-full-drain bins (bin:0,0,0; bin:0,1,0; bin:1,-1,0; bin:1,0,0) — drained variant with drainage holes. Bins filled with soil and planted with basil, parsley, mint, chives seedlings to demonstrate use

finish.summary: Built compact 4-cell seed-starting tray using 4 hex bases each fitted with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain). Applied capOpenFaces and lockJoints, then filled bins with soil and staged with four different seedlings visible from above.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your seed-starting tray needs four draining bins — I'll build a compact cluster to hold them.
